source_title: Sports Manisha Bhanwala Makes History, Becomes India's First Woman Wrestling World Champion
source_excerpt:
Manisha Bhanwala has reached a landmark that no Indian woman wrestler had achieved before her. The 59kg grappler became India's first female gold medallist at the Wrestling World Championships, fighting back from a six-point deficit to defeat American Abigail Nette 8-6 in the final on Friday.
Bhanwala was trailing 0-6 before producing a remarkable turnaround to take the contest and secure the world title. With this victory, she also became only the second Indian wrestler to win gold at the senior World Championships, joining Sushil Kumar, who claimed the men's 66kg freestyle title in 2010.
Her achievement came during an exceptional campaign for India's women wrestlers. For the first time, three Indian women reached the gold medal bouts at the same edition of the World Championships. Neelam Sirohi in the 50kg category and Kajal Dhochak in the 76kg event finished with silver medals on Thursday, while Tanmu Sharma added a bronze.
Born on February 10, 1997, Manisha comes from Siwaha village in Haryana's Jind district, with Rohtak also associated with her early life and wrestling journey. She stands 5 feet 2 inches tall and has competed in multiple weight categories, including 62kg and 65kg, before winning the world title in the 59kg division.
Her development has been shaped by the guidance of coach Mandeep Singh at Sir Chhotu Ram Stadium and Japanese coach Kosei Akaishi at the Inspire Institute of Sport.
Wrestling was not initially part of a long-term career plan. In 2013, her father took her to an akhada to help her lose weight and improve her fitness. That decision introduced her to the sport and eventually set her on the path to becoming a world champion.
Bhanwala's rise through the wrestling circuit began early. She won the Cadet World Championships in 2016 and also secured gold at the South Asian Games that year in the 60kg category.
Two years later, she added another major achievement by winning gold at the World Military Games in China. Her progress continued at the continental level, although the Asian Championships initially brought a series of podium finishes rather than a title.
She won bronze medals at the Asian Championships in 2022, 2023 and 2024. In 2025, she finally reached the top of the podium, claiming gold in the 62kg category in Amman, Jordan.
That victory also came after a difficult final. Bhanwala recovered from a 2-7 deficit to defeat North Korea's Kim Ok-Ju 8-7, securing India's first women's gold at the Asian Championships in four years. She had also won gold at the National Games in Goa in 2023.
Her latest triumph against Nette represents another major step in a career built on recovering from difficult positions. Bhanwala had earlier booked her place in the World Championships final with a commanding semi-final win over Kazakhstan's Altyn Shagayeva.
One of the most difficult periods of Bhanwala's life came in April 2022. Her father died after suffering a sudden heart attack on April 17, the same day she was scheduled to travel for the Asian Championships.
Despite the personal loss, she decided to compete at the tournament. She returned with a bronze medal, having continued her campaign during an extremely difficult period.
Bhanwala also made a significant career decision when she left her job in the paramilitary forces. The demands of the job were affecting the time she could devote to training, prompting her to resign and concentrate fully on wrestling.
She had already attracted attention during selection trials by defeating Olympic medallist Sakshi Malik on three occasions, underlining her ability to compete against established names in Indian wrestling.
The 59kg world title is a major achievement, but Bhanwala's longer-term ambitions extend to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. She is now working towards a move to the 57kg category as she looks to prepare for the next Olympic cycle.
Her height of 5 feet 2 inches has been a consideration in her weight-category decisions. She has spoken about the physical challenge of facing taller European opponents in the 62kg division.
The move to 57kg could therefore become an important part of her preparation for Los Angeles. For now, however, Bhanwala has already secured a place in Indian sporting history. Her comeback against Nette ended the country's long wait for a women's wrestling world champion and gave Indian wrestling a landmark moment on the global stage.

hi_body:
मनीषा भानवाला ने शुक्रवार को कुश्ती विश्व चैंपियनशिप के 59 किलोग्राम वर्ग के फाइनल में अमेरिका की एबिगेल नेट्टे को 8-6 से हराकर इतिहास रच दिया। छह अंकों से पिछड़ने के बाद उन्होंने शानदार वापसी करते हुए भारत के लिए पहला महिला स्वर्ण पदक जीता।

रिपोर्ट्स के अनुसार, इस जीत के साथ वह सीनियर विश्व चैंपियनशिप में स्वर्ण पदक जीतने वाली केवल दूसरी भारतीय पहलवान बन गई हैं। उनसे पहले सुशील कुमार ने 2010 में पुरुषों की 66 किलोग्राम फ्रीस्टाइल श्रेणी में यह उपलब्धि हासिल की थी। इस प्रतियोगिता में नीलम सिरोही और काजल ढोचक ने रजत पदक तथा तन्मू शर्मा ने कांस्य पदक भी अपने नाम किया।

## शुरुआती सफर और पृष्ठभूमि

10 फरवरी 1997 को हरियाणा के जिंद जिले के सिवाहा गांव में जन्मी मनीषा ने साल 2013 में अपने पिता के कहने पर वजन घटाने और फिटनेस सुधारने के लिए अखाड़े जाना शुरू किया था। वर्ष 2016 में उन्होंने कैडेट विश्व चैंपियनशिप और दक्षिण एशियाई खेलों में स्वर्ण पदक जीते। इसके बाद 2022, 2023 और 2024 में एशियाई चैंपियनशिप में कांस्य पदक जीतने के बाद, उन्होंने 2025 में अम्मान, जॉर्डन में 62 किलोग्राम वर्ग में स्वर्ण पदक हासिल किया।

## व्यक्तिगत संघर्ष और करियर के निर्णय

अप्रैल 2022 में मनीषा के जीवन में एक कठिन दौर आया जब एशियाई चैंपियनशिप के लिए रवाना होने वाले दिन ही उनके पिता का दिल का दौरा पड़ने से निधन हो गया। भारी मानसिक आघात के बावजूद उन्होंने प्रतियोगिता में हिस्सा लिया और कांस्य पदक जीता। कुश्ती पर पूरा ध्यान केंद्रित करने के लिए उन्होंने अपने अर्धसैनिक बल की नौकरी से भी इस्तीफा दे दिया था।

## भविष्य की योजनाएं

खबरों के अनुसार, मनीषा 2028 लॉस एंजिल्स ओलंपिक की तैयारी के लिए 57 किलोग्राम वर्ग में जाने की योजना बना रही हैं, जिससे उन्हें ऊंचे कद की प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के खिलाफ होने वाली शारीरिक चुनौतियों से निपटने में मदद मिल सके।

पाठक आधिकारिक खेल बुलेटिनों और खेल निकायों के रिकॉर्ड के माध्यम से मूल घोषणा की सत्यता की जांच कर सकते हैं।

Manisha Bhanwala made history by becoming India's first female gold medallist at the Wrestling World Championships, defeating American Abigail Nette 8-6 in the 59kg final on Friday after overcoming a six-point deficit.

Reports indicate that this victory makes her only the second Indian wrestler to claim gold at the senior World Championships, joining Sushil Kumar, who won the men's 66kg freestyle title in 2010. The tournament also featured notable performances from Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak, who won silver medals, and Tanmu Sharma, who earned a bronze.

## Career Journey and Background

Born on February 10, 1997, in Siwaha village, Haryana, Bhanwala initially entered an akhada in 2013 at her father's suggestion to improve her fitness and lose weight. Her early successes included winning the Cadet World Championships and the South Asian Games in 2016, followed by gold at the World Military Games in China. After claiming bronze medals at the Asian Championships in 2022, 2023, and 2024, she secured an Asian Championship gold in the 62kg category in Amman, Jordan, in 2025.

## Personal Resilience and Career Decisions

Bhanwala faced severe personal hardship in April 2022 when her father passed away from a heart attack on the day she was scheduled to travel for the Asian Championships. She chose to compete and earned a bronze medal. To dedicate more time to her sport, she also resigned from her job in the paramilitary forces.

## Future Aspirations

Looking ahead, Bhanwala is reportedly planning to transition to the 57kg category to prepare for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, aiming to counter the physical challenges of facing taller opponents in higher weight classes.
